stem: public record Person(string Name, int Age); generates all of the following EXCEPT:
explanation: One line yields constructor, properties, equality, hashing, ToString, Deconstruct and with-support. Databases remain your problem.

stem: var a = new Person("Ada", 36); var b = new Person("Ada", 36); What is a == b?
explanation: A record asks 'same data?'; a class asks 'same object?'. ReferenceEquals(a, b) is still false - two objects, equal values.

stem: var older = ada with { Age = 37 }; What happened to ada?
options: Nothing - with produces a modified COPY
explanation: Non-destructive mutation: a new record with one change, original untouched. The core habit of immutable programming.

stem: record Player(string Name, List<string> Items); Two Players with identical names and identical item lists: equal?
options: No - List<string> compares by REFERENCE, and they are two different lists
explanation: Generated equality compares each member with ITS equality - and List's is reference-based. Compare contents with SequenceEqual, or use immutable collections.

stem: Why do records work perfectly as Dictionary keys and in HashSets?
options: Correct Equals AND GetHashCode are generated together, and init-only properties keep them stable
explanation: The 2.10 contract - equal values, equal hashes - comes generated and consistent, and immutability means the hash cannot change while stored (5.9's disaster).

stem: Which should NOT be a record?
options: BankAccount with a changing balance and an identity
explanation: Two accounts with the same balance are NOT the same account - identity plus mutable state wants a class. Data defined by its values wants a record.

stem: readonly record struct Coordinate(int X, int Y) combines:
explanation: Stack/inline storage, no per-instance allocation, plus the generated equality and ToString - ideal for small data copied often.

stem: Can a record have a body with validation and computed properties?
options: Yes - a full body works; positional syntax is just the shorthand
explanation: Records accept constructors that validate (Temperature throwing below absolute zero), computed properties and methods - they are classes with generated extras.

stem: (string first, string last, int age) = ada; works because positional records generate:
explanation: Deconstruct(out ..., out ..., out ...) comes free with positional records - the same mechanism 4.6 writes by hand for classes.

stem: record Employee(...) : Person(...). Does a Person ever equal an Employee with the same values?
options: No - generated equality also checks the exact record type
explanation: Record equality includes an EqualityContract type check, so instances of different record types are never equal - even with matching data.
